DisabledTests.*-TLS1-*: DTLS 1.0 is not supported (RFC 8996 deprecates it)
DisabledTests.*-TLS1: DTLS 1.0 is not supported (RFC 8996 deprecates it)
DisabledTests.*-RSA_WITH_*: Static RSA key exchange is not offered: RFC 9325 §4.1 requires forward secrecy, WebRTC uses ECDHE (RFC 8827 §6.5)
DisabledTests.*_CBC_*: Only AEAD suites are offered (RFC 9325 §4.2; WebRTC requires AES-GCM, RFC 8827 §6.5)
DisabledTests.AppDataBeforeHandshake-DTLS*: Records that cannot be valid are silently discarded (RFC 6347 §4.1.2.7) rather than aborting the handshake
DisabledTests.AppDataBeforeTLS13KeyChange-DTLS*: Records that cannot be valid are silently discarded (RFC 6347 §4.1.2.7, RFC 9147 §4.5.2) rather than aborting the handshake
DisabledTests.SendInvalidRecordType-DTLS: Records of an unknown type are silently discarded (RFC 6347 §4.1.2.7) rather than aborting the connection
DisabledTests.WrongMessageType-NewSessionTicket-DTLS: DTLS 1.2 session tickets are not offered, so the runner never sends the NewSessionTicket this test alters
DisabledTests.TrailingMessageData-NewSessionTicket-DTL: DTLS 1.2 session tickets are not offered, so the runner never sends the NewSessionTicket this test alters
DisabledTests.UnencryptedEncryptedExtensions-DTLS: A plaintext record after handshake keys exist is silently discarded (RFC 9147 §4.5.2) rather than ending the handshake
DisabledTests.DTLS-Retransmit-BothTimers-TLS13*: BoringSSL acknowledges a copy of the HelloRetryRequest; RFC 9147 §7.1 says that flight is acknowledged by the next one and SHOULD NOT be ACKed, and a stateless server's copy says nothing of our flight (§5.1)
DisabledTests.DTLS-Retransmit-PartialProgress-Client-T: BoringSSL keeps resending its ClientHello after a complete ServerHello; RFC 9147 §7.2 requires a record that responds to a flight to be taken as an implicit acknowledgement of it
DisabledTests.KeyUpdate-Requested-DTLS: Asked to update, we acknowledge the KeyUpdate before sending ours, in the order of RFC 9147 Figure 14 and as OpenSSL requires; the runner expects the ACK only on BoringSSL's ACK timer, which this test never fires
